title: Follow-ups: reduce provision-to-ready validation flakes + tune timeouts (NCCL, disk warmup, network jitter)
creator: Harish Reddy
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
- During staged rollout (us-east / A100) we saw a meaningful share of nodes fail readiness due to validation flakiness rather than true hardware/network issues.
- These failures manifest as:
  1) NCCL all-reduce smoke test timing out intermittently (suspected transient fabric jitter / slow GPU init / NCCL algo selection variance)
  2) Disk/storage warm-up effects causing IOPS/latency spikes early in node lifetime, which cascades into runtime smoke/perf canary failures
  3) Network throughput/jitter checks occasionally tripping thresholds (no clear sustained degradation; likely noisy sampling + host-level variability)

Goal
- Reduce false negatives so quarantine is a high-signal action.
- Keep time-to-ready SLOs intact (don’t “fix flakes” by inflating timeouts globally).

Non-goals
- Redesigning the validation framework/state machine (see ADR-017 / ENG-4822).
- Changing cluster topology or scheduler behavior.

Observed failure patterns (rollout notes)
- NCCL:
  - Timeouts skewed toward the first run after node joins cluster; rerun often passes.
  - Failures frequently lack sufficient artifacts to distinguish true fabric issue vs slow start.
- Disk:
  - Nodes that pass later tend to fail when validations run immediately after provisioning; warm-up mitigates.
- Network:
  - Single-sample iperf-like checks are too sensitive; small jitter causes threshold breach.

Proposed work (breakdown)
1) NCCL smoke test: reduce flake, improve diagnostics
- Tune timeout strategy:
  - Use a 2-tier timeout: shorter first attempt, longer retry only if failure looks transient.
  - Consider GPU-type-specific defaults (A100 vs others) behind config.
- Reduce variance:
  - Pin message sizes / iterations to a stable profile for “smoke” (not perf benchmark).
  - Ensure consistent NCCL env settings (e.g., algorithm/protocol) for smoke path only.
- Better artifacts on failure:
  - Capture NCCL debug logs (bounded) and GPU topology summary for failed runs.
  - Record whether failure was timeout vs non-zero exit vs Xid/ECC signal.

2) Disk warm-up + validation ordering
- Add lightweight warm-up step prior to runtime smoke/perf canary:
  - Small fio read/write warm-up (bounded time, low impact) or equivalent to avoid first-touch penalties.
  - Pre-pull critical container images used by validation agent + perf canary to remove registry/network coupling.
- Revisit ordering:
  - If disk warm-up is needed, do it before perf canary; keep it as a separate step with explicit duration metrics.
- Ensure fail semantics are right:
  - If warm-up fails due to transient cloud issues, retry before quarantine.

3) Network jitter checks: make them robust, keep them actionable
- Sampling strategy:
  - Take N samples and use median/percentile rather than a single run.
  - Separate “throughput below floor” from “jitter above ceiling”; treat jitter-only failures as retryable.
- Threshold calibration:
  - Use rollout data to pick thresholds that flag real degradation but don’t trip on normal variance.
- Diagnostics:
  - On failure, attach bounded outputs: ethtool stats snapshot, MTU, driver version, and a short trace ID to correlate with host metrics.

4) Quarantine policy alignment (do not quarantine on known flakes)
- Update the retry/backoff policy for these steps so that:
  - Known-flaky signatures get at least 1 retry before counting toward quarantine.
  - Quarantine requires either repeated failure OR a “hard fail” signal (GPU health / ECC / Xid / driver mismatch).

5) Metrics + dashboards improvements for flake tracking
- Add a first-class “retry_count” and “failure_class” dimension (bounded cardinality) to validation result events.
- Dashboard: “flake rate” = failures that succeed on retry / within X minutes.
- Ensure we don’t regress on cardinality controls (see metric tag incident).

Acceptance criteria
- For us-east / A100 staged pools:
  - Post-provision validation flake rate (fail then pass on retry within 30m) < 0.5% over 7 days.
  - Quarantine rate attributable to NCCL/network/disk validations reduced by 50% vs rollout week baseline.
  - No material increase in provision-to-ready P95 (target: +<= 5 minutes vs current post-sprint baseline).
- For any node that still fails:
  - Failure reason artifacts are sufficient to decide: retry vs reimage vs quarantine vs escalate to cloud provider.

Implementation notes
- Some robustness improvements landed in PR-18481 (agent timeouts/retries/log bundling). This ticket is for the follow-up tuning + step semantics + threshold calibration that we didn’t want to rush during rollout.

Owners / reviewers
- Primary: Gabe Wilson (implementation)
- Infra review: Vanessa Ortiz / Keiko Yamamoto
- SRE review (thresholds/alerts): Aisha Bello / Miles Thornton
- Observability review (metrics cardinality): Allison Grant / Sergio Costa

Open questions
- Should NCCL smoke be mandatory for Ready on all pool types, or only for Dedicated + specific fabrics? (If conditional, where does policy live?)
- Do we want separate thresholds per region (given different underlying network characteristics), or keep global thresholds and accept slightly higher retries in “noisier” regions?

Next steps
- Collect 7 days of step-level failure + retry outcomes from staged rollout dashboards.
- Propose updated thresholds/timeouts in a short design comment, get SRE sign-off.
- Implement behind feature flags so we can roll forward/back per region/GPU type.
comments: 2025-10-18 (Harish Reddy): Creating this as a bucket for the flake items we intentionally deferred while trying to keep the first staged rollout moving. Biggest pain points from ops were repeated NCCL timeouts that pass on rerun, plus perf canary failures that correlate with early disk slowness.

2025-10-19 (Aisha Bello): +1 on separating retryable vs hard-fail. For alerting we should page on sustained quarantine spikes, not on single-step transient failures. Please add a metric for "failure_class" but keep the values bounded (no raw error strings).

2025-10-20 (Vanessa Ortiz): For NCCL: we need more artifacts. Today we can’t tell if it’s a real fabric issue or just startup variance. Let’s capture NCCL debug logs (bounded) + topo summary for failures only. Also please avoid increasing the global timeout unless we have data that it doesn’t hurt P95 time-to-ready.

2025-10-22 (Gabe Wilson): I’ll prototype: (1) median-of-3 sampling for network check, (2) disk warm-up step + image pre-pull, (3) NCCL smoke profile change to reduce variance. Will post proposed thresholds once I pull the last 7 days data from the step breakdown dashboard.

2025-10-24 (Miles Thornton): Reminder: quarantine semantics should remain conservative. If a node fails NCCL twice, I’m fine quarantining, but the first failure should be a retry unless there’s an accompanying GPU health signal (Xid/ECC).
